title: Decomposition Classics: 911, Bank Fraud, Medication Errors
subtitle: Decompose emergency response, bank fraud and medication-safety prompts by mission, evidence and accountable decisions.
author: By Sourav Banerjee

practice_prompts.label: Mission, owners and guardrails
practice_prompts.hint: Name the hidden conflict, the north star and the guardrail that catches its harm.

practice_prompts.label: Input map and riskiest unknown
practice_prompts.hint: Fill shape, owner, freshness, what it can answer and quality risk; say which unknown goes first.

practice_prompts.label: First slice, model and human boundary
practice_prompts.hint: Describe the walking skeleton, the model chosen last and where the human sits.

practice_prompts.label: Evaluation and the curveball
practice_prompts.hint: Backtest, shadow, matched pilot; then re-derive after losing GPS, system C or scanning data.

rubric: I asked at least five clarifying questions whose answers changed the plan before drawing anything.
I named the mission's hidden conflict (equity, customer friction or alert fatigue) and a guardrail metric that would expose it.
My input map had owner and quality-risk columns, and I said what each source cannot prove.
I ordered workstreams by the unknown that could kill the project and justified the order.
My first slice delivered value without a new model (a segmentation report, a single queue, or retrospective reconciliation).
I kept the language model in a bounded, human-confirmed role on free text.
I staged evaluation as backtest, shadow and matched pilot with a held-out labelled set.
When the curveball came, I re-derived the plan and said what coverage was lost instead of defending the old plan.
I narrated my reasoning throughout and finished within the 60-minute clock.

editorial_review.evidence: Re-review on 16 Nov 2026: read all 23 captured sections (dumped to text) against the previous casebook item by item. The previous version kept every source table but thinned the teaching prose badly: the three verbatim prompts table was missing; section 1's narration scoring and second quote, the GPS curveball quote, the universal opener, the input-map 'owner' rationale, the riskiest-unknown sentence for fraud, customers' declined cards, the medication stakeholder list, the 'is AI the right solution' line, the cost-card drivers and the level-calibration framing were absent; the six probes and three two-minute openers were squeezed into two paragraphs; the Quick review dropped most takeaways. It also had wrong captions: in all three deep dives the component table was captioned as failure modes and the failure table as trade-offs, and all six case diagrams had generic 'source figure 1/2' alt text. I rebuilt casebook.md around the existing tables: brief now opens with the prompt table, assumption callout and term definitions, then what the round scores; walkthrough gains a separate sequencing step; each deep dive follows the source's 5.1-5.9 order under h4 headings with figures beside their component tables and prose traces read from the SVG labels; Practice has 22 worked reveals (12 checks, 6 probes, 3 openers, cost); Quick review carries all 11 takeaways. First-person source opinions ('In my experience', 'I'd argue') are attributed to the source. Unsourced additions from the previous rewrite (an 'equity claim' line, softened check answers) were replaced with source wording. Source oddity kept and explained: the cost table had blank headers in the source; given Question/Answer. November 21 complete maintained-baseline review: All five sections: brief and framework, five walkthrough steps, the 911, bank fraud and medication deep dives with their tables and six figures, the comparison and cost card, references, twelve self-checks, six probes, three openers, cost pivot, three level tables and Quick review. Targeted corrections and source-to-output mappings: /Users/sourav/Github_Repos/Forward-Deployed-Engineer-Interview-Prep/.website_spec/casebook-review-24-33-2026-11-21/decomposition-classics-67-68-69/audit.json. Historical captured-source mappings remain preserved; this pass audits the maintained baseline. Source inconsistencies settled in text (2026-11-21): Step 4 names where the 911 minutes go as the riskiest unknown while the comparison table named traffic sensors → the row now names hand-entered call timestamps first and keeps the sensors, because the workstream order starts with segmenting call records..
